description: Fork of exp147 (E=64, qk_tph=384, d_qk=64, real-valued Q/K with LN, attn_scale=0.125, 618M, +0.124 behind exp144 at step 1400 — failed). Single change: qk_mhlut_init_std 0.001 -> 0.05 (50x larger init for the qk_lut only). Hypothesis: with init_std=0.001, qk_lut output magnitudes are ~0.02 = sqrt(tph)*init_std = sqrt(384)*0.001 — even after LN standardization, the random-direction component dominates content-encoded direction at init, so attention weights are content-blind and gradients can't break the symmetry. Larger init makes the LUT output have more substantial random structure that LN can normalize while preserving content-direction signal. Other LUTs (v, out_proj) keep init_std=0.001.
